summary: Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Sydney, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith (1919–2016) worked in religious studies and philosophy, earning degrees from Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Denver, Washington University in St. Louis, MIT, Syracuse University, and UC Berkeley.

Huynh Kim Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hwansoo Kim is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He has held appointments as a professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).
Hwi-Ok Chang (born 1951) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1985 to 1991 and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University around 1995.

Hyakudai Sakamoto (1928–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held academic posts at Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, Aoyama Gakuin University, and the Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 2015) and served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara (attested 2015).

Hyon Gak Sunim (born 1964) is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Yale, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard, and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University, and Jesus College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at Bangor University from circa 1936 to 1955.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He received his PhD from the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (attested 2010) and Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.

Hōun Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Sōji-ji. She was head priest at Unpukuji, founded Shasta Abbey in 1969, and served as its abbess until 1996.

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge and Lancaster. He founded the UKABS and held posts at Lancaster, St Martin's College, St Hugh's College, NUS, and the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate in Asian Studies at La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Yasutani.

Ian Reader (born 1949) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Leeds. He held positions at Kansai Gaidai, Kobe University of Commerce, Stirling, Hawaiʻi, Lancaster, and Manchester.

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned his PhD from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Muhammad Farooq Swati. He has served as Associate Professor and Chairman of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and held academic posts at Otani University Junior College (~1967–1969) and Otani University (~1969–2007).
